title: Amazon’s Streaming TV Pitch to Mid-Market Brands: What Actually Works

facts.fact: Amazon rebranded its Sponsored TV ad product to Streaming TV in 2025, per the page.
facts.quote: Amazon rebranded Sponsored TV to Streaming TV in 2025.

facts.fact: The page states that the self-service Streaming TV door has no minimum spend and uses CPM billing with a daily budget the advertiser sets.
facts.quote: CPM billing, daily budget you set, eligibility requires Brand Registry, and you can launch a campaign in an hour.

facts.fact: The page says eligibility for self-service Streaming TV requires Brand Registry.
facts.quote: CPM billing, daily budget you set, eligibility requires Brand Registry, and you can launch a campaign in an hour.

facts.fact: The page says self-service DSP through Amazon has no stated minimum spend.
facts.quote: Self-service DSP through Amazon has no stated minimum spend

facts.fact: The page reports that agencies typically recommend a starting self-service DSP budget of around $10,000 per month to generate enough impressions for meaningful optimization.
facts.quote: agencies typically recommend a starting budget of around $10,000 monthly to generate enough impressions for meaningful optimization.

facts.fact: The page states that managed-service DSP starts at $50K.
The page cites an Amazon ad spec calling for a minimum video bitrate of 15 Mbps, MP4 format, and durations between 6 and 45 seconds for Streaming TV.
facts.quote: Amazon’s ad spec calls for a 15 Mbps minimum bitrate to maximize supply coverage, MP4 format, and durations between 6 and 45 seconds.

facts.fact: Canopy Management estimates that a purpose-built 15 or 30 second Streaming TV spot, produced well, costs five figures to make, which it calls the real cost floor.
facts.quote: A purpose-built 15 or 30 second spot, produced well, runs into five figures.

facts.fact: Amazon reports, using its own internal data, that customer journeys exposed to Streaming TV alongside other sponsored ads had 58% better New-to-Brand conversion rates than journeys without TV.
facts.quote: Amazon reports that customer journeys exposed to Streaming TV alongside other sponsored ads drove 58% better New-to-Brand conversion rates compared to journeys without TV.

facts.fact: Canopy Management advises that if Sponsored Display spend is under 10% of total Amazon ad budget, that should be fixed before adding Streaming TV.
facts.quote: If your SD spend is under 10% of your total Amazon ad budget, fix that first.

facts.fact: Canopy Management's website claims its partners achieve an average 84% profit increase; this is the vendor's own marketing claim.
facts.quote: Canopy's Partners Achieve an Average 84% Profit Increase!

facts.fact: The page describes its target audience as mid-market Amazon brands doing $150K to $750K a month on Amazon.
